tasks.short: Watch animal and plant environments, and correct what drifts.

steps.what: Read the alarm and the reading that fired it.
Go look at the animal or plant environment.
Log what was wrong and what was done.
Decide the new target after the look.
Write that target onto the controller.

tasks.design: A reading outside the band raises an alarm on {OPS_SYSTEM}. The manager still goes and looks. The response is a short log. A new target is written to the controller only after the manager decides it. The look is the same environment reading used elsewhere.
tasks.previous_blocker: Setpoints lived in a private sheet, and a night alarm depended on who was near the controller.
tasks.enabler_now: A band and a reading are numbers. An alarm is a comparison. The right target after a look is not.
tasks.still_hard: A sensor can be wrong, and a house can be wrong in a way the sensor does not name.
tasks.human_edge: The manager can tell a failed probe from a real problem, and knows what the stock will tolerate.
tasks.altitude: Alarms replace scanning every controller. The look and the new target stay. The manager does not hand the setpoint to the alarm.

reach.task: Act on the log when the manager is off the site
reach.learn: What the alarm was, and what target was written

evidence.claim: An alarm on a numeric band is a comparison a controller can already do. Choosing a new target is not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager looks and decides the target. The controller stores the reading. Accepting a day's readings is a different task.
Structured input: location, measure, reading, band low, band high, time. Producer is the controller. A reading with no location is not alarmed.
Going to look is the bulk of the time and stays.
unknowns: Which houses already have a controller with a band?
research_questions: How often is an alarm a failed probe?

already_counted.description: Going to look is already the remaining time on that step.
Deciding the new target is already remaining time.

incremental.description: Retire bands that no longer match the crop or the stock.

approvals.approved_version: target the manager decided after looking

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If controllers cannot raise an alarm, the manager still walks. Only the log is new. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Arrange finance and purchase machinery, land, supplies or stock.

steps.what: Pull supplier quotes and the cash position.
Draft a funding note from those figures only.

loop.input: the quote table and the cash position
loop.output: a funding note that quotes only those figures
loop.check: every amount in the note must equal a quote or the cash row; else discard
loop.stop: one draft; a missing quote is left blank
loop.why_not_simpler: whether to borrow is not a calculation

steps.what: Edit the note and sign that version.
Meet the lender and discuss that version.
Release the purchase, or send it back.
Send the purchase order to the supplier.

tasks.design: Quotes and cash are a table from {PROCUREMENT}, {ERP} and {BANK}. A funding note is kept only when every amount equals that table. The manager edits and signs it, then meets the lender. The finance manager releases the purchase. The order goes out only after that release. The meeting does not shrink.
tasks.previous_blocker: Quotes were collected by hand, and a purchase could leave before anyone checked the cash.
tasks.enabler_now: Quote lines and a cash balance are rows. A note can be refused when it contains a new number.
tasks.still_hard: The lender's appetite, and whether the machine is really needed, come out in the meeting.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which machine failure would stop a harvest, and the finance manager knows the cash.
tasks.altitude: Collecting quotes takes less time. The meeting stays. The manager does not gain the right to send an order without the finance release.

reach.learn: Which note version and which lender answer they are releasing

evidence.claim: A quote table can be summed. A lender's decision cannot be drafted into existence.
A purchase that commits the firm is an internal control. Who may sign is the firm's own rule, not a feature of the form.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager prepares the note and meets the lender. The finance manager releases the order. The lender's credit decision is outside.
Structured input: item, supplier, quote amount, cash balance, need-by date. Producer is the quote file and the bank balance. A blank amount is not filled.
The meeting is the largest share and stays in full. Finance release time is finance's, and is not counted as the manager's saving.
unknowns: Who may release a purchase above a stated amount?
Are quotes already rows, or attachments?
research_questions: How often is an order placed before the cash is checked?

already_counted.description: Editing the note is already the remaining time on that step.
The lender meeting is already the remaining time on that step.
The finance release is already remaining time on that step.

incremental.description: Retire quotes that have passed their validity date.

approvals.approved_version: release the finance manager recorded for that note version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If quotes are unscanned attachments, the table is typed once and the meeting is unchanged. The order still waits for release. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Alarms send the manager to look. A new target is written only after that look. A purchase still ends in a lender meeting and a finance release.
reach: A worker on the night shift can read the response log.
Finance sees the same quote table.
skills_to_grow: Tell a failed probe from a real problem.
Do not send an order the finance manager has not released.
role.ambitious_version: The controller is not scanned by hand all day, and an order cannot leave ahead of the cash check.

job.title: Farmers, Ranchers, and Other Agricultural Managers
